cards.b: Chord V, built on the fifth note of the scale; creates tension and wants to go to I.
V followed by I (or V7 to I); sounds finished like a full stop.
Ends on chord V; sounds unfinished.
IV followed by I, the Amen cadence; gentler.
V followed by VI, a surprise; avoids the expected ending.
A major chord ending a piece or section in a minor key.
A change of key within a piece.
To the dominant or the relative minor.
To the relative major or the dominant.
A long held or repeated bass note while chords change above it.
A continuous sustained note or fifth, typical in folk music.
A held note from the previous chord that clashes, then resolves downwards by step.
Music with no key centre and no tonic.

gaps.s: Chord I is called the ___ chord.
A V to I cadence is called a ___ cadence.
IV to I is a ___ cadence.
V to VI is an ___ cadence.
A change of key is called a ___.
A long held bass note under changing chords is a ___ note.
Music with no key centre is called ___.

short.q: Explain how a perfect cadence differs from an imperfect cadence.
short.model: A perfect cadence is V to I and sounds finished; an imperfect cadence ends on V and sounds unfinished.
A sustained or repeated note, usually in the bass, held while the chords above change.

short.q: Give two likely destinations for modulation from a minor key.
short.model: The relative major and the dominant.
Dissonant chords or suspensions, chromatic notes, a dominant pedal, or an unresolved or interrupted cadence.
It is the rate at which chords change; slow changes sound calm and fast changes sound busy.
